content.comment_body: Hello, I'm new to [company_name] [product_name] software and am facing challenges with my programming. I have a pool system with two heating sources: solar panels and a heat pump. Since solar heating is cost-free, I want it to have priority when conditions are suitable. Here’s the logic I'm aiming to implement: - Target temperature set for the pool - Temperature sensor 1 (solar panels) - Temperature sensor 2 (pool) - Solar heating should activate if pool temperature is below the target and sensor 1 reads higher than sensor 2 - Heat pump should activate if pool temperature is below target and sensor 1 reads lower than sensor 2 I have managed to set up the function using a fixed set point, but I'm looking for guidance on integrating analog signals from the sensors to select the appropriate heating source. Any advice would be appreciated. Thanks in advance.

analysis.insight_summary: The discussion highlights a user experiencing difficulty with programming pool automation logic that switches between two heating sources and prioritizes solar heating using real-time analog data from temperature sensors in [company_name] [product_name] software. Another participant provides a sample file, indicating that the analog comparison feature might benefit from clearer documentation or a more intuitive programming interface.
analysis.user_expectations: The user hopes to be able to straightforwardly program control logic in [company_name] [product_name] software to select between two heating sources using analog sensor inputs, with an emphasis on prioritizing solar heating whenever possible.
